stories.summary: Prime Minister Takaichi made a ritual offering to the Yasukuni Shrine on April 21, becoming the first direct visit or offering by her government since taking office. stories.headline: Northern Japan Wildfires Force Mass Evacuations; Over 3,000 Residents Displaced
stories.summary: Massive wildfires in Iwate Prefecture in northern Japan forced the evacuation of over 3,000 residents over four days through April 26. More than 1,400 firefighters and 100 JSDF personnel were deployed to contain the blazes, which affected the third-largest area of any recorded wildfire in Japan, threatening the coastal town of Otsuchi.

stories.headline: Magnitude 6.1 Earthquake Strikes Hokkaido; No Damage or Casualties Reported
stories.summary: A magnitude 6.1-6.2 earthquake struck Hokkaido, Japan's northernmost main island, in the early hours of April 26, centered near the town of Sarabetsu. No tsunami was issued, and authorities reported no damage or casualties from the tremor, which struck at a depth of approximately 81 kilometers.

stories.headline: Australian Foreign Minister Wong to Visit Japan for Energy Security Talks
stories.summary: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong will visit Japan, China, and South Korea this week to discuss energy supplies and regional cooperation. The visit comes ahead of Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi's expected visit to Australia in early May, signaling strengthened bilateral energy and security coordination.

stories.headline: Mexico to Supply Japan with One Million Barrels of Crude Oil
stories.summary: Mexico has agreed to provide Japan with one million barrels of crude oil, according to talks between Prime Minister Takaichi and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum held earlier in the week. The agreement addresses Japan's energy security concerns amid supply disruptions from regional conflicts.

articles.title: Mexico to ship 1 mil. barrels of crude oil to Japan

stories.headline: Japan Lower House Passes Bill to Establish National Intelligence Council
stories.summary: Japan's lower house passed legislation on April 23 to establish a National Intelligence Council, positioning it as a 'Japanese CIA' to strengthen state intelligence-gathering activities. The bill, a key policy of Prime Minister Takaichi, won support from both ruling coalition members and opposition parties concerned about privacy and oversight.

stories.headline: Takaichi Pushes Constitutional Reform Agenda to Strengthen National Defense
stories.summary: Prime Minister Takaichi is using her political popularity and the LDP's electoral landslide to advance constitutional amendments, a longstanding party goal she views as essential to Japan's defense modernization. Her April convention speech emphasized the need for constitutional change to address the country's 'most severe and complex security environment' since 1945.

stories.headline: Japan and US-Philippines Conduct Expanded Military Exercise Balikatan 2026
stories.summary: Japan's Self-Defense Forces, alongside approximately 1,400 personnel, participated in the expanded Exercise Balikatan 2026 with US and Philippine forces in April 2020. The exercise, designed to enhance defense interoperability and maritime security, reflects Japan's deepening military integration in the Indo-Pacific region.

stories.headline: JSDF Tank Incident Kills Three Ground Self-Defense Force Members
stories.summary: Three members of Japan's Ground Self-Defense Force were killed on April 21 when a shell exploded inside a Type 10 main battle tank during a live-fire exercise at the Hijudai Training Area in Oita Prefecture. A fourth soldier was injured in the incident, which prompted investigation into the causes of the deadly accident.

stories.headline: LDP Recommends Sending Minesweepers to Strait of Hormuz After Iran Conflict
stories.summary: Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party recommended on April 25 that the government consider sending minesweeper vessels to the Strait of Hormuz once fighting between the US and Iran concludes. The proposal responds to Trump's March request and reflects Japan's strategic interest in maintaining freedom of navigation through the critical energy chokepoint.

stories.headline: Japan Secures Alternative Crude Oil Supply Routes Amid Middle East Conflict
stories.summary: Prime Minister Takaichi held a ministerial meeting on April 25 to address Japan's energy security in response to the Middle East conflict. Japan expects to secure approximately 60 percent of its crude oil needs for May through alternative routes outside the disrupted Strait of Hormuz, demonstrating its preparedness based on past crisis experience.

stories.headline: JS Izumo Carrier Upgrade Progresses with New Rectangular Flight Deck
stories.summary: The Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force released new photographs on April 20 showing the JS Izumo helicopter carrier's upgraded rectangular flight deck, marking progress in its conversion into an F-35B 'Lightning Carrier'. The second-phase modifications advance Japan's carrier strike capability for regional defense.

stories.headline: LDP Security Commission Compiles Recommendations to Strengthen Defense Capabilities
stories.summary: The Liberal Democratic Party's Research Commission on Security began compiling official recommendations on April 22 on how Japan can strengthen defense capabilities and adapt to new forms of warfare. Recommendations include improving the Pacific flank's surveillance, monitoring, and response capabilities, addressing what party members termed a 'defense vacuum'.

articles.title: LDP commission compiling first suggestions to bolster defense

stories.headline: Government and LDP Consider Reducing Maximum SDF Manpower Capacity
stories.summary: Government and ruling coalition officials are mulling reducing the maximum number of Self-Defense Forces members in line with revision of three national security documents this year. Ministry officials indicate current manpower levels are unrealistic for mid- to long-term sustainability, with even LDP lawmakers acknowledging that reduction is unavoidable.

stories.headline: Japan's Core Inflation Remains Below BOJ's 2% Target in March
stories.summary: Japan's core inflation slowed below the Bank of Japan's 2% target for the second consecutive month in March 2026, as government fuel subsidies and moderating food inflation offset price pressures from the Iran war-induced energy shock. The BOJ, which exited stimulus in 2024 and raised rates in December, continues monitoring inflation dynamics.

stories.headline: Japan Launches Financial Sector AI Cybersecurity Task Force
stories.summary: Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama announced on April 24 that Japan will establish a task force to address cybersecurity risks in its financial system following concerns about potential vulnerabilities linked to advanced AI models. The task force involves the Financial Services Agency, Bank of Japan, National Cybersecurity Office, major banks, and Japan Exchange Group.

articles.title: Japan launches financial task force amid AI security fears

stories.headline: Takaichi Faces Fresh Pressure Over Reported Rift with Key Security Ally
stories.summary: Japanese media reported on April 25 that Prime Minister Takaichi is facing growing pressure following a worsening rift with a close confidant over security and foreign policy. articles.title: Japanese PM faces fresh pressure amid reported rift with close ally
